takeaways: Text can be enlarged to 200% without losing content or function.
Design for growth: containers expand, text wraps, nothing is clipped.
Avoid fixed heights on anything that holds text.
On phones, respect the system text size setting.
failures: Text cut off or overlapping when enlarged
Fixed-height buttons that clip two-line labels
Layouts that only work with one line of text
check: Zoom the browser to 200% and use the page.
Set your phone to its largest text size and open the app.

quiz.question: At 200% text size a tab label is cut off with an ellipsis, and there is no other way to read it. Does it pass?
options: Yes. Truncation is a standard pattern
quiz.why: If the full label cannot be read, content is lost. Let it wrap, or let the tabs scroll.

spec: Show how each component grows: wrap, expand or scroll.
Mark containers as hugging their content, not fixed height.
Include a large-text version of key screens.
review: What does this screen look like at the largest text size?
Where will long translations break this layout?
tradeoff: Tight, pixel-perfect layouts break first. Flexible layouts look a little less controlled and survive real use, including translation.
system: Build components with auto layout and test each one at 200% before release.
pitch: Many people run their phone at a larger text size. A layout that breaks under it breaks for them every day.
